company: DLR Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics
company_native: Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt, Institut für Robotik und Mechatronik
target_applications: research: household/service mobile manipulation, space telerobotics (ISS-to-ground avatar)

base_type.value: wheeled, 4 independently steered spring-suspended wheels on extensible legs (variable footprint), 8 platform DoF

torso_lift.value: 3-DoF articulated torso (pitch joints), no lift column

actuators.value: harmonic-drive torque-controlled joints (LWR-III lightweight arm technology), link-side torque sensors in nearly all joints

end_effector.value: 2x DLR Hand II four-finger dexterous hands, 12 DoF each, fingertip torque sensing

sensors_head.value: 2 stereo camera pairs, 5 RGB-D cameras (system total), 2-DoF neck; earlier 3DMo head with stereo + laser-stripe + IMU

sensors_wrist_hand.value: joint torque sensing throughout arms and fingers (41 link-side torque sensors)

software_stack.value: DLR in-house real-time middleware, Matlab/Simulink toolchain; teleop via force-feedback exoskeleton, tablet UI, scalable-autonomy task-level commands (Surface Avatar); no public SDK

safety_compliance.value: none (research platform); intrinsic safety via torque sensing/impedance control

availability.value: not available; one-off DLR research platform

deployment_evidence.value: METERON SUPVIS-Justin ISS teleop 2017 (Nespoli); Surface Avatar ISS campaign 2023-2025 (Rubio, Dyson/Epps, Kim) concluded successfully; famous catching/coffee demos

notes: Agile Justin (2012) variant: ~1.5x faster arms, new bus/wheel electronics, throwing capability. Technology lineage: LWR-III -> KUKA LBR iiwa; alumni founded Franka Emika, Agile Robots. runtime_h given as '>60 min' by DLR.
